meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here, Hale. I have about twenty minutes, so tell me why my son has a zero.
Hale, I didn't come to be thanked. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that nothing about this be placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a visit to the principal's office.
What moved her: nothing, since you gave her no evidence or ownership of the process.
What cost ground: "Thanks for coming in," because it gave her nothing to check and left her question about who decided the zero unanswered.
Try next time: in your first sentence, own that the zero went in before you called her, then put a dated document in front of her.
